mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to turn negative due to tightened financial conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite the rate increase, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in monthly employment (PAYEMS) above the prior month's value is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return, reflecting optimism about labor market strength.
failure_condition: No significant return advantage over 60 days after the employment surge, or negative returns persist despite multiple consecutive months of gains in PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by over 2% signals weakening supply-side demand, which predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >2% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat despite the large drop in INDPRO, or the effect is not robust across multiple contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising residential housing starts (HOUST) above trend are associated with a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as it signals economic expansion and consumer confidence.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > HOUST previous month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant positive returns in the 5-day window following the boom signal, or the effect is only observed in non-recessionary periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% suggests disinflation, which drives a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically better than the prior month's average during disflation periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) by over 10% in a month is interpreted as a labor market softening, predicting a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive despite the large drop in benefits claims, or the effect is not significant in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer demand proxy (RSAFS) by at least 1% each month indicate dual softening, which predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < INDPRO previous month AND RSAFS < RSAFS previous month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite simultaneous declines in both proxies, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% for 2 consecutive months indicates labor market tightness, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as investors anticipate wage growth.
failure_condition: No positive 5-day forward return during the identified tightness period, or the effect is only present in non-recessionary regimes.
